Class Hopper

public class Hopper extends edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.SubsystemBase
Hopper subsystem â€” two motors that move balls from the storage area into the shooter.

Mechanism Overview

The hopper has two stages:
  • Indexer (m_hopperMotor): belt or wheel mechanism that advances balls through the storage area toward the kicker. Typically runs at lower speed to pace ball delivery.
  • Kicker (m_kickerMotor): final accelerator stage that launches the ball into the shooter flywheel at the right entry speed. Runs at full speed (positive duty cycle).
The two speeds can differ â€” the negative indexer speed (âˆ’0.9) and positive kicker speed (+1) in ShootWhenReady reflect a reversal in the mechanism geometry: the indexer belt runs "backward" (negative) to push balls forward.

Integration with ShootWhenReady

ShootWhenReady calls startAllMotors(double, double) from inside a startEnd command. The startEnd pattern guarantees that stopAllMotors() is called when the command ends or is interrupted â€” critical in autonomous to prevent the hopper from running into the next path segment after a shot timeout expires.

Note on IO Layer

Unlike the turret and shooter, the hopper does not use an IO interface. It drives the TalonFX motors directly with percent-output duty-cycle control (.set(speed)), which is sufficient for this open-loop application â€” no position or velocity feedback is needed for ball feeding.

      public void startAllMotors(double hopperSpeed, double kickerSpeed)
      Starts both motors at the specified duty-cycle speeds.

      Typically called from startEnd inside ShootWhenReady with hopperSpeed = âˆ’0.9 (indexer belt reversed into shooter) and kickerSpeed = +1.0 (kicker at full speed).

      Parameters:
      hopperSpeed - indexer duty cycle (âˆ’1.0 to +1.0); negative = toward shooter in this geometry
      kickerSpeed - kicker duty cycle (âˆ’1.0 to +1.0); positive = launching into flywheel

    • stopAllMotors

      public void stopAllMotors()
      Stops both motors immediately.

      Called by the startEnd end block in ShootWhenReady whenever that command ends â€” whether normally, via timeout, or via interrupt. This prevents the hopper from running uncontrolled between auto path segments.
